content.text:
Asks now all run at the same time, a single row each, stacked above the tabs. Running asks no longer dim the message list. 92 of 93 tests pass; the one failure is the palette test that was already failing. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I haven't tried several real asks at once in the running app.

**How it works now:**
- **Asking:** each ask starts straight away as its own row, newest nearest the tabs, and sliding up as before. A new ask no longer stops or replaces one already running. I skipped a queue, since running them all at once covers it.
- **Finishing:** when an ask finishes, it opens onto its full table. Only one is open at a time; opening another shrinks the open one back to a row.
  - Click an open ask's heading to shrink it back to a row showing its status and first line.
  - Click that row to open it again.
- **Closing:** each row has its own X, which stops that ask if it's still running and leaves the others alone.
- **Dimming:** the message list dims only while a finished answer is open, never for running rows.

**Shared conversation:** asks still carry on one ask conversation. If an ask starts while another is already running, it carries on a copy of the conversation (`--fork-session`), so two runs never write to the same session at once. The catch is that the copy's follow-up context isn't merged back. The ask that started last decides which conversation the next ask picks up.

**One thing to watch:** several open rows plus an open answer can stack tall and cover a good part of the message list. Rows don't have a height limit yet.

**Tests:**
- The existing ask tests now work with a list of asks.
- A new test checks that two asks run at once and stack newest-last above the tabs, and that neither dims the list.
- It also checks that a finished ask opens and closes, and that closing one ask leaves the other running.

**Spec:**
- `ChatInputScope`: several asks at once, stacking, opening and closing.
- `MessageList`: dimming only for an open answer.
- `HarnessIntegrationScope`: copying the conversation for asks that run at the same time.
